Bounty Hunter.desc: Licensed or freelance retrieval specialist. You get paid when the target is in cuffs—or a slab.

benefits.title: Dead or alive paperwork
benefits.effect: You can always identify local bounty-posting customs and typical bond rules without a roll (who pays, who enforces, what voids a claim).

benefits.title: Pressure at range
benefits.effect: +1 to Intimidation against a single target who knows you are armed and serious (once per scene per target).

benefits.title: Hunter’s mark
benefits.effect: In the first round of combat, once per combat, shoot at a target that has not acted this round; each raise adds 1d6 to damage.

benefits.title: Guild hall tone
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion or Streetwise (pick each roll) when dealing with organizations that routinely work with hunters: bounty guilds, posting authorities, law-enforcement liaisons, or prison and transport contractors.

Colonist.desc: Frontier settler, ag worker, or town pillar. You know how to make a life where supply lines are thin.

benefits.title: Community face
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion when dealing with locals in a settlement of ≤ 5,000 people.

benefits.title: Practical medicine
benefits.effect: +1 to Healing when treating shock, heatstroke, dehydration, or vermin bites—not lightsaber wounds or major surgery.

benefits.title: Barter sense
benefits.effect: You always know who runs the local market, who sets landing pad fees, and who will trade favors for food or parts (no roll to learn that gossip).

benefits.title: Co-op voice
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion or Streetwise (pick each roll) when dealing with organizations rooted in settlement life: homestead councils, agricultural co-ops, colonial administration, or frontier relief and supply leagues.

Hired Gun.desc: Mercenary, enforcer, or line soldier for credits. Violence is the job description.

benefits.title: Suppression habit
benefits.effect: +1 to Shooting on your first attack in a firefight after you or an ally has already been Shaken or Wounded this combat (represents covering fire timing).

benefits.title: Mercenary rep
benefits.effect: You recognize unit insignia, typical contract rates, and which officers actually pay on time—no roll for general knowledge of merc bands in the Outer Rim.

benefits.title: Heavy familiarity
benefits.effect: Ignore 1 point of multi-action penalty when your extra action is only bracing, deploying, or swapping to a heavy weapon you personally own (GM discretion).

benefits.title: Contract floor
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion or Streetwise (pick each roll) when dealing with organizations that trade in force: mercenary companies, PMC contracting desks, arms suppliers, or veteran and muster societies.

Smuggler.desc: Blockade sprinter, fixer, or fast-talking loader. Cargo flies if the story holds.

benefits.title: Gray manifest
benefits.effect: +1 to Thievery or Streetwise when hiding contraband in a vehicle, crate, or false panel you prepared at least one scene in advance.

benefits.title: Yeah, I'm sure you have...
benefits.effect: Once per scene, if you are in a conversation with the target, you may attempt to draw your blaster and attack. Roll Thievery; on a success, you have the Drop on that target for the attack.

benefits.title: Fixer’s introduction
benefits.effect: In any starport Class III or larger, you know a fence, loader’s union rep, or corrupt clerk by reputation; the GM names them when you arrive.

benefits.title: Gray channel
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion or Streetwise (pick each roll) when dealing with organizations that routinely touch the shadow trade: fences, blockade-runner rings, dockside syndicates, or black-market clearing houses.

Technician.desc: Ship’s engineer, slicer, or grease-stained genius. If it has wires, you’ve sworn at it professionally.

benefits.title: Battlefield patch
benefits.effect: +1 to Repair when fixing something damaged in the last hour during combat or an active chase.

benefits.title: Bad Motivator
benefits.effect: Spend a Benny and roll Repair at −2; on a success, a technical item spontaneously ceases to work until it is fixed. Droid Extras are Shaken instead.

benefits.title: Spare tub
benefits.effect: Once per scene, make a Repair roll (0 to 4 penalty, GM discretion) on a technical item you own; on a success, you have a spare of that item. If you fail, you damage the item until it is repaired.

benefits.title: Yard cred
benefits.effect: +1 to Persuasion or Streetwise (pick each roll) when dealing with organizations that keep ships and machines running: shipyards, mechanics’ unions, factory service desks, or certified repair and parts networks.
